record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: Given a finite group G and a normal subgroup H, does there exist a low-depth noisy quantum circuit that maps the quantum double phase associated to G to the quantum double phase associated to H?

evidence.quote: Question 15 Is there a low-depth noisy quantum circuit that maps the quantum double phase associated to a finite group G to the one associated to a normal subgroup H?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite group and let H be a normal subgroup of G. For any finite group K, let D(K) denote Kitaev's quantum double model defined on a 2-dimensional lattice: the local Hilbert space on each edge is C[K], and the Hamiltonian is the standard sum of mutually commuting vertex operators (enforcing gauge invariance under K) and plaquette operators (enforcing flatness of the K-gauge connection). The ground space of D(K) realizes the topological phase whose anyon content is the Drinfeld center Z(Rep(K)).

A "low-depth noisy quantum circuit" is a quantum channel obtained by composing a number of layers, independent of the system size (or growing at most poly-logarithmically), where each layer is a tensor product of local quantum channels (CPTP maps) acting on O(1)-sized regions of qudits, possibly using ancillas and measurements with classical feed-forward.

Question: Does there exist such a low-depth noisy quantum circuit Φ that maps the quantum double phase associated to G to the quantum double phase associated to H? More precisely, does there exist a constant-depth (or poly-logarithmic-depth) local quantum channel Φ such that Φ sends any ground state of the D(G) Hamiltonian to a state in the topological phase of D(H), implementing the anyon condensation associated with the inclusion of the normal subgroup H ⊴ G?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search shows active research on related questions—anyon condensation via locality-preserving channels, mixed-state topological order under decoherence, and adaptive constant-depth circuits for non-Abelian quantum doubles—but no source explicitly resolves the general question of whether a low-depth noisy circuit can map the D(G) phase to the D(H) phase for an arbitrary normal subgroup H ⊴ G. Status appears unresolved in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Anyon Condensation and the Color Code
status_evidence.snippet: Studies anyon condensation processes implemented via local operations within color-code/quantum-double settings.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not settle the general G-to-H normal-subgroup question.

status_evidence.title: Noisy Approach to Intrinsically Mixed-State Topological Order
status_evidence.snippet: Abelian topological order undergoing anyon condensation under locality-preserving quantum channels yields new mixed-state phases.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial results on locality-preserving channels implementing condensation, mainly Abelian.

status_evidence.title: A Universal Circuit Set Using the S3 Quantum Double
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs adaptive constant-depth circuits to manipulate non-Abelian quantum double models.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates feasibility of low-depth circuits for specific non-Abelian doubles, but not the general G→H mapping.
